q: What is the minimum period for which a fixed deposit can be opened in India?
explain: Banks accept fixed deposits for a minimum period of 7 days.

q: Which of the following is NOT a part of the money market?
explain: T-bills, commercial papers and certificates of deposit are money market securities. A general mutual fund is not a money market instrument.

q: Which term describes the difference in value between a country's imports and exports?
explain: Balance of trade is the difference between the value of exports and imports. Balance of payments is a wider record of all transactions.

q: If the rupee depreciates, how are exporters affected?
explain: A weaker rupee converts each dollar of export earnings into more rupees, so exporters gain.

q: Which derivative contract gives the holder the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell the underlying asset at a predetermined price within or at the end of a specified period?
explain: An option is a right, not an obligation. Futures and forwards oblige both parties to complete the deal.

q: The market for buying and selling precious metals such as gold and silver is termed:
explain: Trading in gold and silver takes place in the bullion market.

q: Which of the following types of issues are made in the primary market?
explain: Primary market activities include public issues (IPO, FPO), private placement, preferential issue, QIP, rights issue and bonus issue.

q: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: NASDAQ is an American stock exchange
Nikkei is the stock market index of the Tokyo Stock Exchange
S&P CNX Nifty is the index of 50 large companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange
Hang Seng records daily changes of the largest companies of the Hong Kong stock market
explain: Nifty is the 50-company index of the National Stock Exchange, not the Bombay Stock Exchange.

q: What is the gilt-edged market?
options: The market for software technology services
The market for safe securities such as government securities
explain: Gilt-edged means very safe. Government securities carry practically no default risk, so their market is the gilt-edged market.

q: A rise in the Sensex means:
options: A rise in prices of shares of all companies registered with the BSE
An overall rise in prices of shares of all companies on the NSE
An overall rise in prices of shares of a group of companies registered with the BSE
A rise in the price of one company's shares
explain: The Sensex tracks a basket of 30 large companies listed on the BSE; it does not cover every listed company.

q: In which year was the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) established?
explain: BSE was established in 1875, making it Asia's oldest stock exchange.

q: Consider these statements. Statement 1: Nifty is based on 50 companies. Statement 2: Nifty is governed and regulated by the Reserve Bank of India. Which is correct?
explain: Nifty tracks 50 companies of the NSE. Stock exchanges are regulated by SEBI, not RBI.

q: Consider these statements about India INX. Statement 1: It is India's first international exchange. Statement 2: It is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Bombay Stock Exchange. Which is correct?
explain: India INX, located in the IFSC at GIFT City, is India's first international exchange and a subsidiary of BSE.

q: Which statement best distinguishes the primary and secondary markets?
options: Primary markets help capital formation, while secondary markets provide liquidity to investors
IPOs are undertaken in the secondary market only
Stock exchanges are examples of the primary market
Secondary markets issue securities for the first time
explain: Companies raise money in the primary market (IPOs); the secondary market, the stock exchange, lets investors sell and exit.

q: In which year did the World Bank issue its first green bond?
explain: The World Bank issued its first green bond in 2008 to fund climate-friendly projects.

q: Which of the following correctly describes the objectives of the Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC)?
options: To act as an apex forum for financial stability and improve inter-regulatory coordination
To regulate only the stock market
explain: FSDC is an apex-level forum to strengthen financial stability and promote coordination between regulators and financial sector development.

q: Money market securities have a maturity of:
explain: The money market deals in short-term securities with maturity of less than one year.

q: Why is the yield on money market securities generally low?
options: Their short maturity and low risk of loss make them liquid and safe
They are issued only by private firms
explain: Short maturity gives high liquidity and low volatility. Safer and more liquid instruments pay a lower return.

q: How does a common person usually invest in the money market?
explain: Ordinary investors generally reach the money market through money market mutual funds.

q: When did the Securities Transaction Tax (STT) come into effect?
explain: The Securities Transaction Tax Rules were notified in 2004 and STT took effect on 1 October 2004.

q: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) is levied on:
explain: STT is charged on transactions on stock exchanges at rates fixed by the Central Government from time to time.

q: Which of the following is another name for the primary market?
explain: The primary market, where companies issue securities for the first time, is also called the new issue market.

q: When people say "stock exchange", which market do they actually refer to?
explain: A stock exchange is where already issued securities are traded, so it is the secondary market.

q: In which market must a company carry out a buyback of its own shares?
explain: Already issued shares trade in the secondary market, so a buyback has to be done there.

q: Which of the following is NOT a type of primary market issue?
explain: A repo is a short-term money market instrument. Rights, QIP and preferential issues are primary market activities.

q: What do the letters FPO stand for in the context of the primary market?
explain: FPO means Further Public Offer or Follow-on Public Offer, a later issue by an already listed company.

q: Who are the intermediaries in a financial market?
options: Agencies such as banks, brokers, custodians and depositories that connect lenders and borrowers
explain: Intermediaries collect funds from lenders, pass capital to borrowers and handle securities for both sides.

q: In a financial market, borrowers are those who:
options: Are in need of funds or in capital deficit
explain: Borrowers have a capital deficit and obtain funds through the market and its intermediaries.

q: Why would an economy without a financial market be inefficient?
options: Lenders and borrowers must find each other by self-search
Interest rates would always be zero
explain: Without a market, each lender and borrower has to search alone, so many miss the chance to invest or borrow.

q: Which of the following pairs of retirement products covers government and private employees?
explain: Employees of government and private companies are covered under NPS, EPF or PPF; many self-employed people are not covered.

q: Which of the following is a general insurance product?
explain: Motor, health, fire and personal accident covers are general insurance. Term, endowment and whole life plans are life insurance.

q: In India, forex trading is permitted only in:
explain: Indian law permits forex trading only through currency derivatives, under RBI and SEBI control.

q: Which of the following is NOT a currency pair available for derivative trading in India?
explain: The pairs listed for derivative trading are USD-INR, EUR-INR, GBP-INR and JPY-INR.

q: Which market is considered the most liquid of all financial markets?
explain: Because it deals in currencies, the forex market is the most liquid, which is why traders and speculators like it.

q: Which of the following is a commodity exchange of India?
explain: NCDEX is the National Commodity and Derivatives Exchange. The other options are a depository, a credit bureau and the insurance regulator.

q: What does MCX stand for?
explain: MCX is the Multi Commodity Exchange, trading bullion, metals, energy, spices and more.

q: Which authority has regulated commodity derivatives in India since the Forward Markets Commission was merged with it in 2015?
explain: FMC was merged into SEBI in 2015, so SEBI regulates commodity derivatives. FMC was the answer in older exam papers.

q: G-Secs are called gilt-edged instruments because they:
options: Carry practically no risk of default
explain: A government security acknowledges the government's debt and has practically no default risk, hence risk-free and gilt-edged.

q: State Governments in India issue which of the following G-Secs?
options: Both treasury bills and dated securities
Only dated securities, called State Development Loans
explain: Only the Centre issues both T-bills and bonds. States issue dated securities called SDLs.

q: Treasury bills are G-Secs with an original maturity of:
explain: T-bills are short-term securities under one year. Dated securities have an original maturity of one year or more.

q: Floating Rate Bonds (FRBs) were first issued in India in:
explain: FRBs, which have no fixed coupon rate, were first issued in India in September 1995.

q: Which G-Sec protects both the coupon and the principal against inflation?
explain: Inflation indexed bonds protect both coupon and principal, using WPI or CPI. Capital indexed bonds protect only the principal.

q: What does STRIPS stand for?
options: Separate Trading of Registered Interest and Principal of Securities
Secured Trading of Regular Interest and Premium of Shares
Standard Treasury Rates in Public Securities
Separate Taxation of Registered Income and Profit of Stocks
explain: STRIPS separate each coupon and the final principal of a regular G-Sec into individual securities, essentially zero coupon bonds.

q: Which bonds have their principal linked to an accepted index of inflation, to protect the investor's principal?
explain: In capital indexed bonds the principal moves with an inflation index. Only the principal is protected.

q: Which RBI-introduced system lets participants trade G-Secs anonymously through an order-matching screen?
explain: NDS-OM (Negotiated Dealing System, Order Matching) is an anonymous, order-driven electronic system introduced in August 2005.

q: NDS-OM-Web was launched by RBI to allow direct participation of which group on NDS-OM?
explain: NDS-OM-Web, launched on 29 June 2012, lets gilt account holders participate through their primary members.

q: Which of the following is the main regulator of India's primary and secondary securities markets?
explain: SEBI regulates the primary and secondary markets (stock exchanges). IRDAI covers insurance and PFRDA pensions.

q: Which regulator designed the structure of pension products such as the NPS?
explain: PFRDA regulates the pension sector and decided the constituents of the National Pension System.

q: FIMMDA was incorporated as a company under the Companies Act, 1956 on:
explain: FIMMDA was incorporated on 3 June 1998 as a voluntary market body for the bond, money and derivatives markets.

q: FIMMDA is best described as:
options: A voluntary market body for the bond, money and derivatives markets
explain: FIMMDA is a voluntary association of banks, financial institutions, primary dealers and insurers. It introduces benchmark rates and links members to regulators.
